brief.headline: Blackstone lands €13bn for European direct lending
bullets: Private Credit: Blackstone has closed on €13bn (£10.9bn) of investable capital for its European direct lending strategy, as more investors look to private credit on the continent.

Private Markets: Senior executives from Leonard Green & Partners, Hamilton Lane, Carlyle and Bain Capital have defended the growing use of continuation funds, arguing that the structures provide liquidity and support longer-term value creation despite investor concerns over potential conflicts of interest.
Family Offices & Wealth: A Fort Worth team left UBS with $3.61 billion in assets to launch Cleros Wealth Partners, with backing from Elevation Point and custody through Goldman Sachs.

Earnings & AUM: Apollo Global Management’s assets under management increased 18% year-on-year to $1.07tn in the third quarter of 2026, supported by $53bn in new inflows and continued institutional demand for private credit and alternative investments, according to a report by Reuters.

Macro & Geopolitics: Spanish energy group Moeve, majority-owned by Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund Mubadala and backed by private equity firm Carlyle, has agreed to sell its Algerian oil assets to Indonesia’s state-owned energy company Pertamina, according to a report by Reuters.
brief.marketRead: Bottom line: signals are mixed, with some markets calm and others showing strain, so expect selective risk-taking. The S&P 500 stands at 7,568.92 (up 0.4% on the prior reading) and the VIX is 20.8, an elevated reading that signals nervous markets. The effective fed funds rate is 3.88%, the 10-year Treasury yield is 4.91% (down 3 bps on the prior reading) and the 10Y–2Y yield curve is +0.34 pts (positively sloped). High-yield credit spreads are 3.40%, near long-run norms (down 3 bps on the prior reading).
